events.title: Threads Tell Stories: How Archaeologists Read Andean Textiles
events.display_title: Threads Tell Stories: How Archaeologists Read Andean Textiles
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: What can a piece of cloth tell us about the people who made and used it? Using contemporary Andean textiles, alongside images from archaeological research, visitors will be encouraged to look closely at fibers, threads, weaving techniques, colors, and patterns and discuss how these details can help archaeologists understand technology, identity, labor, and everyday life in the past. Become a “textile detective” as you consider what clues different materials and manufacturing choices can provide about the people and communities that produced them. Presented by Rosa María Varillas, PhD Candidate in Anthropology, University of Illinois Chicago; Scientific Affiliate, Field Museum.

This series connects the Field Museum’s research, collections, conservation, and associated community with professionals at the forefront of life, geophysical, and social sciences. events.title: Tlingit Artist James Johnson: Haa Shagoon—The Path Forward
events.display_title: Tlingit Artist James Johnson: Haa Shagoon—The Path Forward
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: As part of Native American Heritage Month, join us for an evening conversation with James Johnson. James will discuss his artistic practice, the importance of preserving traditional Tlingit ways of creating, and how he draws on the knowledge and work of his ancestors in his contemporary practice. James Johnson is an award-winning Tlingit Artist and Carver, born and raised in Juneau, AK. He belongs to the Tlingit Ch’áak’ Dakl’aweidi Clan (Eagle Killerwhale). James is a multi-disciplinary artist but specializes in Tlingit formline design, with a focus on traditional wood carving. Carving is an integral part of the preservation of Tlingit history and culture. “Carving is our visual language that represents who the Tlingit people are, and how we live in balance with all things.” James’s contemporary practice builds upon an indigenous artistic continuum while honoring the culture and its rich traditions. This event takes place on a Legendary Late Hours day and is included with admission. The event takes place in the Montgomery Ward Lecture Hall, on the lower level.

events.title: Black Hawk Performance Company
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Join us for a performance in celebration of Native American Heritage Month with the Black Hawk Performance Company. The Black Hawk Performance Company seeks to honor the ground we dance on, Mother Earth and the many tribes who have made Illinois their home. Many tribes like the Ojibwe, Odawa and Potawatomi and numerous others  have been here for thousands of years and are still here now. Most American Indian people, 70%, live in urban areas like Chicago now. The most famous American Indian leader of historic times was the great Sauk Chief Black Hawk. His name comes from the great black hawks that we see all over the state. We honor both his name and our brother the hawk when we say these words. The Black Hawk Performance Company is a sponsored by the American Indian Association of Illinois.

events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Join the Field Museum for Exploring Indigenous Ingenuity in Ancient Americas , a professional development workshop presented in celebration of Native American Heritage Month . Educators will investigate how Indigenous peoples across the Americas developed scientific knowledge and technological innovations through close observation, experimentation, creativity, and relationships with the land. Participants will engage in inquiry-based, hands-on activities that explore Indigenous ingenuity through a STEAM lens . The workshop will connect ancestral innovations to living Indigenous communities, contemporary knowledge, and cultural identity. Open to formal and informal STEAM educators of all grade levels . Illinois educators will earn 3 Professional Development hours . Registration includes workshop materials and museum admission.

events.title: Mongolian Fossil Plants
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Come join Fabiani Herrera, Negaunee Associate Curator of Paleobotany, as he reveals the mysteries behind 120-million-year-old fossilized plants from Mongolia through the use of a Scanning Electron Microscope. Examine different parts of these fossil plants under the Scanning Electron Microscope and Wentzscope to reveal the tiny secrets that shaped the Age of Dinosaurs and beyond! Discover the characteristics of these ancient plants that connect them to some of their modern relatives and help scientists map their evolutionary lineage.
